transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-27
Start time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Lena Cho (Redwood SE), Dr. Maya Singh (Crestline - Head of ML), Carlos Rivera (Crestline - Cloud Eng), Aisha Khan (Crestline - Security)

Summary (auto): Weekly POC check-in for Redwood Private VPC pilot. Reviewed recent perf benchmarks, discussed networking/egress failures, TLS handshake timeouts observed in last test, KMS access questions, and plan for next round of load testing. Agreed on next steps and owners.

Topics: performance results, routing / VPN vs private endpoint, KMS/key rotation, model upgrade/quantization testing, canary routing, perf run schedule

Transcript:
[00:00] Samir: All right, everybody, thanks for joining. Quick roll call; I see Maya, Carlos, Aisha, and Lena — great. Agenda is same as last week: results review, network things, and next perf run.
[00:28] Maya: Yep hey, thanks Samir. Quick note: we ran the smoke test overnight with the small dataset, and saw some timeouts around 3am but not sure if that's infra or routing.
[00:45] Lena: ok, we captured logs — the errors looked like TLS handshake timeouts to our private endpoint, and there were a couple of 503 spikes around the p95. I have the traces pulled.
[01:05] Carlos: to add, our egress path goes through a NAT gateway in our mgmt subnet; we saw a brief route flap when our BGP session to the transit went into reconverge. could that explain the handshake?
[01:22] Lena: yes it could; if the route to the Redwood private endpoint was momentarily unreachable the client side TLS might retry and hit the timeout. we also saw a pattern where larger payloads (batch size 8) increased handshake+setup latency.
[01:40] Aisha: this raises the KMS question again — during the failing windows, do you still need access to our KMS for key unwrap? we want to make sure there are no IAM throttles.
[01:55] Samir: good point. for the private deployment we use customer-managed KMS for the model artifacts and optionally for request-level token encryption. if there are IAM rate limits that could manifest as crypto timeouts. Lena, did we see any KMS error codes?
[02:12] Lena: I looked; most of the stack traces show a socket-level timeout before the KMS call. but there were a couple of downstream exceptions labeled "access denied" in one trace — likely a temporary credential got stale in one worker.
[02:30] Maya: hmm we rotate keys frequently; could be coincidence. Carlos, did you see any credential refresh failures?
[02:38] Carlos: I did see an expired credential in one instance — our automation rotates a short-lived role that the worker assumes; one node didn't refresh properly due to an IMDS delay. we'll patch that.
[02:52] Samir: ok that explains the access denied. technically that would show up as an application-level error, not TLS handshake, but the route flap plus a stale credential could compound.
[03:10] Lena: on perf numbers — from the benchmark yesterday: p50 around 80ms for single-request generation (seq len ~512), p95 around 320ms, p99 ~640ms, throughput about 120 tokens/sec per GPU in the current quantized setup. when we increased batching to 4 we saw p50 -> 140ms and p95 -> 450ms but throughput improved 1.8x.
[03:40] Maya: those numbers are helpful. our SLA target for the beta is 200ms p95 for short prompts; so with batch=1 we're fine but throughput is low. we need to tune between cost and latency.
[03:58] Samir: yes — that's the classic tradeoff. we can propose an autoscale policy that spikes to dedicated capacity for peak and uses batching+caching at lower load. also we can enable prefix caching to reduce repeated token computation for your repeated prompts.
[04:18] Carlos: can you clarify prefix caching — does it require an open KV cache in our VPC or is it managed by Redwood?
[04:26] Lena: it's managed by the runtime but pins caches to the same pool; in private mode the KV cache runs in the customer's VPC as a service in the private subnet we provision. access is limited to the inference instances and encrypted at rest.
[04:43] Aisha: and audit logging for cache hits? we need to audit for PII exposures.
[04:50] Lena: yes audit logs are emitted to your cloud logging; we can filter and redact tokens. we'll follow your retention and export controls.
[05:05] Maya: ok great. next, model upgrades — we pushed a quantized 4-bit profile last week. any regressions?
[05:14] Lena: small drop in quality on certain long-hallucination prompts — human eval score dropped ~2 points on our set. tradeoff was 35% cost improvement. We recommend running evals on your prompt set before rolling to canary.
[05:34] Samir: agreed. we can do a canary route where 10% of requests go to quantized model, 90% to full precision, and compare metrics for a week.
[05:45] Carlos: That sounds good. One operational ask — when we do canary routing, can Redwood route by source ip or by user token so we tie requests back to our internal experiments?
[05:56] Lena: we support routing by header token or by API key id; source IP is less reliable over NAT. easiest is a header tag you set per experiment, and we'll route accordingly.
[06:10] Maya: on networking changes we asked you last week for a network diagram with exact CIDRs to allow our infra to pre-approve routes. Samir — can you send that?
[06:21] Samir: yes I'll send updated diagram with two suggested CIDR blocks and the private endpoint IP ranges after the call.
[06:27] Carlos: pls include the TLS certificate rotation cadence — we need to import the CA into our trust store.
[06:33] Samir: will do. we'll include cert rotation notes and a guide to accept the certs or use mutual TLS.
[06:40] Aisha: on compliance docs — last time you mentioned SOC2 + ISO docs were available. we need the audit logs retention options and whether we can disable logs for certain data sets.
[06:52] Samir: we have SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 artifacts; for private deployments, we can configure log routing and retention in your stack — we don't force retention. we'll share docs.
[07:05] Lena: quick note on the TLS handshake timeouts — one mitigation while Carlos patches the IMDS refresh is to increase client-side TLS timeout to 10s for retries to hide transient route flips. not ideal but buys time.
[07:20] Carlos: ok we can temporarily increase that. also we'll re-run the overnight test after we provision the additional test subnet.
[07:29] Maya: for the perf run schedule, how about the next full run on 2026-06-03 with the 1k concurrent user profile?
[07:36] Lena: that's fine. we'll coordinate to reserve extra GPUs in the dedicated pool for that window to avoid noisy neighbors.
[07:45] Samir: note that reserving capacity will have a short term cost bump; we'll send options (burst vs reserved) in the email.
[07:54] Aisha: one security question — you mentioned HSM integration. Do you support Cloud HSM or bring-your-own HSM appliances for the private offering?
[08:04] Samir: we support cloud KMS and HSMs; for on-prem you can integrate via the KMIP connector and we can use your HSM for key unwrap. we'll need network access and an ops process for rotation.
[08:18] Carlos: good. another small item — we've seen unexpected 429s during heavy runs; do you throttle per API key or per IP in the private deployment?
[08:27] Lena: in private deployments throttling policy is configurable; by default we throttle per route and per model pool to protect a shared pool. since you're using a dedicated pool for the pilot, 429s would indicate the pool is at capacity; we can increase pool size or add autoscale policy.
[08:43] Maya: were the 429s correlated with the BGP flap windows?
[08:49] Lena: partly — some 429s were immediate downstream backpressure from failed retries, so they are correlated but not identical.
[08:58] Samir: ok let's recap the immediate actionables: I'll send the network diagram and cert rotation guide; Lena will run the 1k perf benchmark on 2026-06-03 and share p50/p95/p99 logs; Carlos will provision test subnet and fix IMDS refresh patch; Aisha will validate KMS access and share IAM policy.
[09:20] Maya: +1. Also please include the canary rollout plan for the quantized model so we can sign off.
[09:27] Lena: we'll include canary config (10/90 split, header-based targeting, fallback policy) in the doc.
[09:35] Carlos: timeline question — if the perf run on 06-03 looks good, how quickly can we flip production? we have a quarterly release window in mid-June.
[09:45] Samir: with canary and a successful perf+quality check we can propose a production flip in 2 weeks post-run, so mid-June fits but depends on your release approvals.
[09:58] Aisha: one more for the security review — we want to ensure audit logs for model prompts are redacted before storage to avoid PII retention. is redact-before-write supported?
[10:10] Lena: yes we support pre-ingest redact rules; we can apply your regex-based sanitizers before logs land in storage. we'll include examples.
[10:23] Maya: perfect. any blockers we didn't cover?
[10:29] Carlos: none from infra after I do the IMDS fix and add the test subnet.
[10:35] Aisha: none from security besides the KMS confirmation which we'll get back on.
[10:40] Samir: great. Recap of next steps and owners?
[10:45] Maya: go ahead Samir.
[10:48] Samir: Samir -> send network diagram + cert notes by 2026-05-29; Lena -> run perf on 2026-06-03 and share results; Carlos -> provision subnet + patch IMDS by 2026-05-28; Aisha -> confirm KMS/HSM access by 2026-05-31. Also Samir will attach SOC2/ISO bundle and pricing options for bursting vs reserved capacity.
[11:10] Maya: thanks everyone, that timeline works. we'll reconvene after the perf run for a decision.
[11:18] Samir: thanks — ending early as we covered everything.
